BiblicalUsage: The eagle in Daniel is a picture of height and of falling: Nebuchadnezzar's hair grows like eagles' feathers when he is driven from men, and the first beast of the vision has eagle's wings that are plucked away before it is made to stand like a man. The eagle's height is borrowed, and it is taken away.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that every high thing in Daniel's visions is brought low on purpose — the eagle's wings are plucked so that proud men learn to stand as men.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
